milestone: WP-01 bounded destination batch name-group assessment
build_interpretation: Initial Mac six-step build/test took 6.814/0.883 s, including CMake configuration and compilation of the new core and both fixtures. Final two-step deterministic-fixture update took 3.407 s and tests 0.891 s. Core and native fixture source remained unchanged between those builds. Compiled/linked input records and source/output hashes establish freshness, not elapsed time.

Linux expanded build/test took 7.483/0.171 s; Windows 21.651/3.423 s. Both compile the new core and both new fixtures. The prior different name-rule expanded Windows workload took 15.463 s; the new simulator/state-machine fixture is larger. No unchanged/no-op build is substituted for compilation of changed inputs.

Focused diagnostics compile all 34 configured core units, one platform adapter, two new fixtures and test host (38 units) directly from source with no object-cache inputs. Mac build/test took 55.261/0.327 s; Linux 135.470/0.074 s; Windows 79.039/0.219 s. The preceding different 37-unit name-rule fixture set took 52.305/118.198/67.413 s. This new fixture set has its own baseline.

Final executable hashes and per-host timestamps were retained before diagnostics were checked for live owners/empty fixture roots and removed. Current normal builds remain. Mac scratch stayed on S8T and Windows development stayed on V:. No GUI was launched.
guarantees: The assessment retains the whole sealed batch and its actual parent, preserving original names, mapping errors, exact groups, held occupants and separate object-alias observations. It performs no new child lookup, pathname reopen, content access or mutation.

All rows and mapped component byte limits are validated before new location I/O. Summary construction is linear; pair/row access uses sealed exact-group indices without name rescans or a quadratic pair table.

Exact groups remain lexical facts. Distinct-group evidence requires a fresh qualified applicable native rule. Unknown/denied/changed/failed rules remain explicit, and hard-link identity cannot become name equivalence.
Zero or one mapped group needs no policy query. None refers only to other mapped groups and does not clear duplicate groups, unmapped source errors or existing-target conflicts.

Separate location-query phases commit replies before cancellation/time yields; resumption never repeats completed native I/O. Exceptions, backwards clocks and resource failures poison private staging. Issued results retain owners independently after job abandonment.
limitations: This is name-group evidence, not a frozen plan, namespace snapshot, name acceptance, absence, object inequality, permission or execution-time collision proof. Old batch occupant observations are not refreshed. Parent/rule/current-occupant revalidation and native exclusive publication remain required.

Policies not qualified by the native name-rule boundary remain unresolved here, including current Darwin/Windows and other Linux filesystem policies. Native positive group qualification is exercised on the Linux ext4 scratch filesystem; other filesystem qualification is not claimed.

Native location calls may block beyond cooperative slices. Row/component limits are resource bounds, not a process-memory or OS-handle guarantee. Successfully mapped destination components use this job limit; unmapped source data remains governed by the original batch bounds.

No macOS LeakSanitizer coverage is claimed. WP-01 remains incomplete for remaining native policies/capabilities, preservation inventories, large-view indexes, UI/worker ownership and execution safety. WP-02..08 remain required.
